outline.chapter_title: Governing Legal Standards for Third-Party Consent Searches
outline.description: This section outlines the constitutional framework applicable to the case, explaining the Fourth Amendment warrant exceptions regarding consent searches performed by third parties with common authority. It details the standards for determining whether consent was voluntary under the 'totality of the circumstances' test and defines the objective reasonableness standard used to evaluate the scope of such consent.

outline.chapter_title: [Analysis] Scope of Consent and Final Disposition
outline.description: This final chapter examines whether the officers' actions inside the home stayed within the boundaries authorized by Lisa's consent. It analyzes how checking child welfare justified scanning rooms and locating occupants, rendering alternative arguments like exigent circumstances unnecessary. The chapter concludes with a summary of holding and remarks on police discretion in domestic settings.
